7	
8	=== RHEA 2026-10-14 21:04 ===
9	That's the London's whole reputation. It's easy to set up and easy to go dead in. The setup is
10	the same every game, so the plan has to come from the position, and the opening never hands you
11	one. What does the board usually look like at move 15? Who's castled where?
12	
13	=== DAMON 2026-10-14 21:06 ===
14	both castled short. my bishop on d3, knight on e5 usually, queen on f3 or e2. their stuff is
15	all just kind of there
16	
17	=== RHEA 2026-10-14 21:07 ===
18	Then you've got the standard kingside setup and you're not using it. Knight on e5 and bishop on
19	d3 are pointing at h7. The usual plan from there is f4, Rf3, Rh3, and a queen swing. It's crude
20	and it works at club level more often than it should.
21	
22	=== DAMON 2026-10-14 21:08 ===

24	
25	=== RHEA 2026-10-14 21:09 ===

27	you lose slowly to someone who has one. Try it for ten games and see what actually happens
28	instead of what you're afraid happens.
29	
30	=== DAMON 2026-10-14 21:11 ===

37	Early c5 against the London changes the plan. They're hitting d4 before you've finished
38	setting up. The quiet answer is c3, holding the center and keeping the bishop's diagonal. The
39	sharper answer is dxc5, giving up the center for development, and that suits you less.

41	=== DAMON 2026-10-14 21:15 ===

43

45	Qb3 and offer the trade. If they take, you get an open a-file for your rook and their queen is
46	off the board, which takes a lot of the danger out of their play. If they don't take, they've
47	spent a tempo to look at your pawn.
